result.text:
`POST /import` now handles quoted fields, so a name like `"Müller, Hans"` stays in one column. The full suite passes: 111 tests, 0 failures, up from 104. I did not run it with a real warehouse CSV.

**Cause:** `src/legacy/csvImport.ts` splits every line on `,`, so a comma inside quotes shifted all the later columns. That file is vendored and overwritten every Monday, so I left it untouched. `git status` shows no changes under `src/legacy/`.

**Fix:**
- **New parser:** `src/lib/csv.ts` is a quote-aware parser. It also handles `""` as a literal quote, quoted line breaks, CRLF line endings and blank lines.
- **Import route:** `src/routes/import.ts` now calls it instead of the legacy parser.
- **Same behaviour otherwise:** the parser keeps the legacy header, the defaults (service `standard`, country `AT`) and the carrier-code mapping, because it reuses `legacy/carrierCodes.ts`. Error line numbers still count after the header and skip blank lines.

**Tests:** `test/csv.test.ts` is new. It covers the parser, including a row where both the name and the street contain commas. It also covers an end-to-end import of `"Müller, Hans"` that checks the stored name and city.

**Things to know:**
- **Legacy parser:** `parseLegacyCsv` is still used by one existing test in `test/import.test.ts`, but nothing in the app uses it any more.
- **Unclosed quote:** a quote that is never closed swallows the rest of the file into one field. In practice that shows up as a validation error on that row rather than a crash.

texts: The bug is in `src/legacy/csvImport.ts`, which is vendored and off-limits. I'll read it and the import route, then put the fix outside `legacy/`.
I'll leave the vendored parser alone and add a quote-aware parser in `src/lib`. It will reuse the legacy carrier mapping, and the import route will use it instead.
The failure is in my test data, not the parser. The tracking number I made up has a wrong check digit, and the validator caught it. I'll use `RR123456785AT`, which is valid.
